critique: The black field, luminous amber color, and fine Form particle texture are convincing. Frame 1 is a reasonably compact fluid mass, but its silhouette remains folded and irregular rather than reading as one rounded drop. More importantly, the motion is still much too disruptive: by frame 4 the mass has stretched into a large porous plume with a long, nearly detached upward tendril and a dispersed lower body. This does not preserve the cohesive, stable Single Drop character.

suggestions.why: Greatly reduce the dominant horizontal fluid flow that is pulling the initially compact drop into a broad, stretched plume over the short frame interval.
Reduce vertical flow so the fluid does not rapidly elongate and separate into an upper tendril and lower cloud.
Lower vortex strength to suppress the strong rolled curls and the detached-looking upward filament at frame 4.
Increase viscosity to hold the particles together as a denser, smoother, more unified drop while retaining restrained internal motion.
Reduce random swirl X so the outer particle field remains attached to the core instead of becoming porous and laterally ragged.
